statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. The Nasdaq-100 complex is inside the CME weekend halt, so no quoting price path exists in any hour of this horizon and Tail is held at a closed-venue floor.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold at a closed-venue floor of 4-5%, so the deterministic mapping holds EA_ON and green across all 24 published hours. Stress drifts from 38% to 46%, crossing into the elevated band only in the final hours, to reflect hawkish September rate pricing and a Strait of Hormuz energy premium that is carried unpriced across the halt. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 unquoted at 29,544.15 through the CME weekend halt; the full 24-hour horizon ends thirteen hours before the Sunday restart, so Tail holds a closed-venue floor while hawkish rate pricing and a Hormuz energy premium accumulate unpriced
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed the August payroll session on Friday 4 September at 29,544.15, up 61.85 points or 0.21% from a 29,482.30 previous close, having ranged between 29,440.15 and 29,655.22. Price retraced repeatedly in both directions during that session, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure the Tail score measures. The August employment report, verified against the Bureau of Labor Statistics release, showed nonfarm payrolls up 162,000 against a consensus near 56,000, the unemployment rate unchanged at 4.1%, average hourly earnings up 0.3% on the month to $37.75 and 3.1% on the year, and upward revisions totalling 55,000 to June and July. Reuters reported the priced probability of a quarter-point increase at the 15-16 September FOMC meeting at 58.4%, up from 49.4% the previous day, while the H.15 release confirms the two-year Treasury yield at 4.34% and the ten-year at 4.77% through 3 September. Index internals were split rather than aligned: the Nasdaq-100 rose while the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.29%, the S&P 500 fell 0.38% and the Dow fell 0.51%, with the narrow index carried by semiconductor and memory leadership. Conflicting breadth of that kind reduces directional conviction and lifts Stress; it is not evidence of the one-way path Tail is defined against. The VIX settled at 14.53 inside a 13.80-14.58 range, indicating the options market did not price disorderly repricing even on a hot payroll day. The material unpriced input remains energy: WTI is quoted near $91.48 and Brent near $92.68 after weekly gains of roughly 10% and 7.6%, the strongest week since mid-July, driven by renewed US-Iran military exchanges and Strait of Hormuz disruption that cut transits to four vessels on Thursday against a ten-day average of fifteen, with US retail diesel at a record $5.85 per gallon. No new verified weekend escalation has been identified as of this assessment. Every hour of this horizon, from 10:00 UTC on Saturday 5 September to 09:00 UTC on Sunday 6 September, falls inside the CME weekend halt, which began at 21:00 UTC on Friday and ends at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, thirteen hours after the final published slot. Tail is therefore held at a 4-5% closed-venue floor throughout, Stress drifts from 38% to 46% to reflect the rate and energy repricing awaiting the restart, and Confidence decays from 85% to 76% purely as Friday's verified evidence ages.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours cover the second half of the August payroll session and the first thirteen hours of the weekend halt. Tail ran 17% with Stress climbing from 60 to 62 through the pre-release European hours, peaked at Tail 24% and Stress 76% in the 12:00 UTC release hour under an event/whipsaw mode as the 162,000 payroll print landed against a consensus near 56,000, then decayed through the US cash session as the index fully retraced its highs and recovered. Mode moved to mixed from 15:00 UTC as semiconductor leadership diverged from a softer broad tape, and by 20:00 UTC Tail was 12% with Stress at 48%. From the 21:00 UTC CME settle the assessment moved to a closed-venue floor of Tail 5% and Stress 38%, held unchanged through the overnight and early Saturday hours. No hour required a mapped state beyond WATCH.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt, so no observable Nasdaq-100 price path can form in any published hour and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON throughout. Tail is held at a 4-5% closed-venue floor, easing to 4% through the dormant middle of the weekend and returning to 5% as the horizon tracks back toward the venue timeline. Stress drifts from 38% to 46%, crossing into the elevated band only in the final hours, reflecting hawkish September rate pricing and a Strait of Hormuz energy premium that lifted crude roughly 10% on the week and is carried unpriced across the halt. Confidence decays from 85% to 76% as Friday's verified evidence ages. The Sunday 22:00 UTC restart, the Monday 7 September US Labor Day holiday, and the PPI and CPI releases on 10 and 11 September all fall beyond the final published hour and will be scored by later cycles against live evidence.
